implementation_notes: The standard library's LazySequenceProtocol is the built-in answer: closure-taking operations such as map and filter are normally eager and return a new array, but reached through .lazy they store the closure and the base sequence and defer computation until elements are needed, which the standard library documents as a way to avoid needless storage allocation and computation. prefix/first end the traversal early, and reduce or Array(lazyChain) is the explicit consumption/materialization point. The permission to defer applies only where the static type is known to conform to LazySequenceProtocol, which is why .lazy must appear before the adapters.
code_sketch:
let total = people.lazy
    .filter { $0.age > 18 }
    .map(\.score)
    .prefix(100)
    .reduce(0, +)          // one pass, no intermediate arrays
pitfalls: Forgetting .lazy on one link makes that step eager: Sequence.map/filter return a new array, so the chain materializes where you thought it streamed.
Lazy wrappers are not memoized and the base sequence must outlive the chain; escaping a lazy sequence that captures a temporary is a lifetime bug.
Each step is a generic wrapper with a closure call per element: for short chains over small arrays the eager version is faster and clearer.

variants.name: AsyncSequence with for await (Swift 5.5+)
variants.idiom_name: AsyncSequence adapters consumed with for await
variants.implementation_notes: When the source is asynchronous, AsyncSequence is the fusion-safe shape: an async iterator produces elements one at a time with await, stages compose with the same adapter vocabulary (map/filter/prefix on AsyncSequence), and for await consumes the pipeline in a single pass without buffering. The design is SE-0298, implemented in Swift 5.5. Use it when stages must await I/O or a producer (network, sensors, pagination); for synchronous data the lazy adapters are cheaper.
pitfalls: AsyncSequence iteration is tied to structured concurrency: cancellation is cooperative, so long-running pipelines must check Task.isCancelled or honour cancellation in their own adapters.
Element production is serialized per iteration; awaiting heavy work inside a stage serializes the pipeline instead of parallelizing it.
AsyncSequence values are single-pass like iterators: sharing one sequence between two consumers requires an explicit buffering/teeing layer.
